---
created: 2026-07-01
description: A note laid out for a screen of electronic paper.
---

Reading on a screen of electronic paper is closer to reading a book than to reading a phone. The page does not glow; it reflects the room's light, and it stays still until you turn it.

That stillness is the point. Nothing slides in from the edge, nothing fades, and a page that has been drawn costs nothing to keep on the screen. What costs is the change, a slow flash from black to white and back again.

So a page for such a screen should change as little as it can. It should be grey on grey, with type large enough to read at arm's length and lines far enough apart that the eye finds the next one without searching.

It should also be turned rather than scrolled. Scrolling redraws the screen many times a second; a turn redraws it once. The reader taps the right edge to go on and the left edge to go back, or presses the page keys of the device.

None of this hides the text from anyone. A screen reader reads the note from its first word to its last, as it would any other page, and a link reached with the tab key brings its page into view.
